provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: A background cell becomes the marker colour when four line segments point at it with a one-cell gap. That means the cells at distances 2 and 3 in each of the four orthogonal directions (up, down, left, right) must all be the line colour. This is the full set of four orthogonal directions, so the condition is unchanged under every D4 rotation and reflection. No axis or direction needs to be rewritten, and the scan works directly in visible coordinates on rectangular grids. Under the palette map, the colour roles become constants: background = palette[8], line colour = palette[1], marker = palette[4]. Cells within 3 of an edge cannot qualify, because the required cells would lie outside the grid. The generator also requires the centre to be background; draw() rejects the scene otherwise. Every qualifying centre is marked, so ties do not arise.
draft_notes.limitations: This has not been tested by me. The roles come from the palette constants, not from inspecting the demos. That assumes the episode's palette argument is the one actually applied. No constructor defects were found: the generator scans centres in the range 3..size-4, which matches the in-bounds check here. No fixture contradicts the rule.
